name: Dolben
type: Multifamily owner and operator (The Dolben Company), 70+ communities and 16,000 units.

Onsite teams film tours themselves, with regional in-person training and ongoing reinforcement because of turnover. name: Gene B. Glick Company
type: Privately held multifamily ownership, development, and management firm (Indianapolis, IN). 21,000+ units across 13 states; founded 1947.
newsQuery: "Gene B. Glick" OR "Glick Company" (apartment OR multifamily OR Indianapolis)
notes: Uses Realync Virtual Leasing and Video Tools (Grace Hill) at 25 conventional apartment properties. Whitespace: Training for leasing and onsite teams; Mystery Shopping and Surveys to measure tour and resident experience; Reputation Mgmt; Policies for the video and brand standards; Market Analysis (Hello Data).

name: Akara Living
type: Multifamily real estate development and property management (Miami, FL). $1.5B assets under management; 12 years in business.
newsQuery: "Akara Living" OR "Akara Partners" (apartment OR multifamily OR Miami)
notes: Uses Realync Virtual Leasing and Video Tools for two goals: cutting maintenance work orders with video tutorials for common requests, and reducing in-person tours with unit-level and amenity video on listing sites (ILSs) and SiteMaps. Launched Kenect Nashville and Sora (formerly Kenect Phoenix). Customer ROI math (customer-reported): 3,048 work orders x 15 minutes = 762 hours (about 32 workdays) of maintenance time over 12 months across 1,000 beds, with appliance, GFI, HVAC, and general maintenance requests making up 35% of service requests. Estimated savings: 1,100 fewer work orders, about 272 hours (about 11 workdays). The 15-minute average would give about 275 hours, so the 272 figure is slightly off from its own inputs. Tours: prospects watch a video for 30 seconds to 1 minute before deciding, versus about 45 minutes for an in-person tour. Results: 1,462 views across 56 videos, about 1,000 from in-unit tours on ILSs and SiteMaps. Sora's living-hacks videos reached 624,000+ likes. Whitespace: Training for maintenance and leasing teams (the work-order problem is a training problem too); Policies for resident self-service rules; Surveys and Reputation Mgmt for resident satisfaction; Mystery Shopping for tour quality; Credentials/CEC; Market Analysis (Hello Data).

name: HILLS Properties
type: Luxury A and A+ multifamily developer, owner, and manager across Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana (Cincinnati, OH). 6,800 units; 210 employees; founded 67 years ago.
newsQuery: "HILLS Properties" (apartment OR multifamily OR luxury OR Cincinnati)
notes: Uses Grace Hill Reputation Management, chosen after vetting multiple vendors and implemented about four years ago. Pulls data from resident surveys and online reviews, and uses risk monitoring, the Local Brand Visibility (LBV) score, Google Maps ranking data, and Pulse AI sentiment analysis. Accountability routines: response-rate monitoring, reminders for property managers with pending reviews, a property-manager session at the Leadership Summit, and a monthly Morning Marketing Power Hour. Results (customer-reported). 2022 to 2023: review volume up 104% (364 to 741), response rate up from 44% to 88%, average rating up from 4.2 to 4.4, and 1-star reviews down 37% (113 to 71). 2024: overall rating 4.5, 718 reviews, a 90% response rate, and over 595 five-star reviews. Also named: Sara Hendricks, Vice President of Property Management, and Stacy Lonsbury, Portfolio Support Specialist, who handle policy compliance, training, and operational integrity. Whitespace: Policies and Training for property management and onsite staff, Surveys (resident feedback is already a data source; confirm current use), Mystery Shopping, Virtual Tools, Market Analysis (Hello Data), and Credentials/CEC.
